brief.title: Boring databases win
brief.goal: Engineers pick a plain relational database for their next new service.
brief.audience: Four hundred backend engineers excited about new distributed databases.
brief.bigIdea: The most boring database is usually the fastest path to a reliable product.

points.text: Most services never outgrow one Postgres node
points.example: 92% of our 140 services use under 50 GB
Three outages last year came from one new store

points.text: You can migrate later when the numbers demand it
points.example: We moved one service after 4 years

brief.openingLine: Our most reliable service runs on a database older than half of this room.
brief.closingLine: For your next service, start boring, measure, and move only when the numbers force you.

issues.problem: The brief never names what excites this crowd about distributed databases. Add the one claim they trust most, then answer it directly.
issues.action: Add one line naming their strongest reason for distributed stores, then counter it.

issues.problem: Point three shows one migration but not the numbers that triggered it.
issues.action: Add the specific metric or threshold that told you it was time to move.

issues.problem: The idea favors boring choices but never says what counts as boring.
issues.action: Add a short definition or example of what makes a database boring.
